entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cornelius Fuscus (b. unknown, d. 86 CE) was a Roman administrator and military commander of the Late Empire era, active in the Roman Empire.


Fuscus rose through the ranks of the Roman military, eventually becoming a prominent figure in the Imperial Guard.


His tenure as commander of the Imperial Guard was marked by his role in suppressing the Bar Kokhba revolt, a Jewish rebellion against Roman rule.


Despite his military successes, Fuscus's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by his contemporaries, and he remains a relatively minor figure in historical accounts of the Roman Empire.
